heroLead: Green Hills sits near Canonsburg in one of the most heavily leased parts of Washington County, where nearly every family farm has some kind of gas history by now.
intro: Green Hills is a small Washington County borough near Canonsburg, in a part of the county where Marcellus leasing swept through so thoroughly over the past fifteen years that it's rare to find a family farm here without some form of gas involvement. That density is a double-edged sword for owners — more activity to draw value from, but also more complicated pooling and deduction questions.
We buy mineral and royalty interests near Green Hills, whether you're managing an active producing interest or trying to make sense of a lease that's been quietly renewing for years.

sections.heading: A heavily leased stretch of the county
paragraphs: Because this area saw an early and thorough leasing wave, many Green Hills-area tracts have been under lease for well over a decade, some producing, some still waiting on their turn in a development schedule.

sections.heading: Sorting out what your lease actually says
paragraphs: With leases this old, terms around post-production deductions, pooling authority, and renewal conditions vary widely, and we read the actual document rather than assuming a standard structure applies.

sections.heading: What we offer and why
paragraphs: We factor in producing status, lease specifics, and nearby well performance, and explain our reasoning clearly before you decide anything.
If your lease terms turn out to be more favorable than typical for the area, that's reflected in what we can offer.

faqs.question: Is Green Hills a good area for Marcellus mineral value given how developed it is?
faqs.answer: Development density generally means more production history to evaluate, which can support a clearer valuation, though actual value still depends on your specific lease terms and unit performance.

faqs.question: My Green Hills lease is over a decade old. Is it still valid?
faqs.answer: It depends on held-by-production and renewal language in the specific lease, which we review before discussing a purchase.

faqs.question: Do you buy interests that are still just leased, not yet producing, near Green Hills?
faqs.answer: Yes, leased-but-undeveloped interests are common in this area given how much leasing activity happened here, and we review those the same as producing interests.

faqs.question: If my Green Hills lease has auto-renewed for years, does that change my royalty terms?
faqs.answer: Not usually — renewal typically extends the lease term under its original terms unless the lease itself allows for renegotiation, so we read the specific renewal clause before assuming anything has changed.
